record.original_question: Is every positive even integer greater than 2 expressible as the sum of two prime numbers?

evidence.quote: The Goldbach conjecture asserts that every positive even integer greater than 2 is the sum of two prime numbers. Despite considerable efforts, this conjecture remains unproven till date.

artifact.self_contained_problem: A prime number is an integer p ≥ 2 whose only positive divisors are 1 and p. Prove or disprove: for every even integer n > 2, there exist prime numbers p and q (not necessarily distinct) such that n = p + q.

status_evidence.title: Goldbach's conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Goldbach's conjecture is one of the oldest and best-known unsolved problems in number theory and in all of mathematics.

artifact.status_search_result: The binary Goldbach conjecture is a well-known unsolved problem in number theory. While Helfgott (2013) proved the ternary version, the binary form remains open as of the current date.
